children: , the commercial-aircraft and defense giant, delivered 51 aircraft in August, 3.8% fewer than in July and 10.5% below last year's level. Investors shrugged off the slowdown, sending the stock approximately 1.3% higher to $215.075 Tuesday.

The company shipped 41 737 MAX jets but just four 787 Dreamliners, down from nine Dreamliners in August 2025. Boeing has now delivered 54 Dreamliners this year while holding to its target of 90 to 100. Hitting the midpoint would require another 41 handovers over the final four monthsan average of more than ten per month.

That execution test matters because Boeing produced only $631 million in quarterly free cash flow despite sitting on a record $715 billion backlog. The market appears willing to treat August's softer total as a timing issue, but the valuation leaves limited room for another stumble: Boeing's $215.075 share price stands 1.87% above its GF Value estimate of $211.13. The next four months must turn that confidence into aircraft, cash and proof that the delivery engine is accelerating.

title: Boeing Rises Even as August Deliveries Fall 11%
